edges.description: ALT sustains replicative immortality and supports continued tumor cell division
Unrestrained malignant smooth muscle proliferation produces a space-occupying soft tissue sarcoma mass.
Rapidly proliferating higher-grade tumor populations drive local recurrence and distant metastatic spread.
Loss of myogenic differentiation in higher-grade tumors is associated with an increased rate of distant metastasis.
Distant metastatic dissemination produces clinically overt metastatic disease.

nodes.description: Loss-of-function ATRX alterations drive a recombination-based, telomerase-independent telomere maintenance mechanism (ALT) in a subset of leiomyosarcomas. The ALT phenotype is enriched in ATRX-mutated tumors and associates with poorly differentiated morphology, tumor necrosis, and worse overall survival.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted next-generation sequencing of cancer genes identified frequent TP53 and ATRX mutations in leiomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: All of the ATRX-mutated leiomyosarcomas showed the alternative lengthening of telomere phenotype.

nodes.description: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy remains a standard first-line systemic option for metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma.

evidence.snippet: First-line therapy for metastatic and/or unresectable leiomyosarcoma includes anthracycline or gemcitabine based regimens, which provide a median progression-free survival time of about 5 months and overall survival time between 14-16 months.

nodes.description: Leiomyosarcoma is capable of both local recurrence and distant metastasis, whereas regional lymph node metastasis is rare, leading to distant metastatic colonization especially in higher-grade tumors.

evidence.snippet: It is capable of both local recurrence and distant metastasis, while lymph node metastasis is rare.
With higher-grade lesions, the rate of distant metastasis increases.

nodes.description: Gemcitabine-based regimens are also used in metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma, particularly when anthracycline therapy is unsuitable or after prior treatment exposure.

evidence.snippet: First-line therapy for metastatic and/or unresectable leiomyosarcoma includes anthracycline or gemcitabine based regimens, which provide a median progression-free survival time of about 5 months and overall survival time between 14-16 months.

nodes.description: Poorly differentiated leiomyosarcoma can progressively lose classic smooth muscle features and overlap morphologically with undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma. This phenotypic drift is accompanied by loss of conventional muscle markers.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive loss of myogenic differentiation in leiomyosarcoma has prognostic value.
evidence.snippet: Well-differentiated leiomyosarcomas show morphologically recognizable smooth muscle differentiation, whereas poorly differentiated tumours may form a spectrum with a subset of undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcomas.

nodes.description: Leiomyosarcoma has a strong propensity for distant metastasis, especially in higher-grade tumors and advanced disease.

evidence.snippet: With higher-grade lesions, the rate of distant metastasis increases.

nodes.description: Radiation is commonly used as an adjunct to surgery for local control, particularly when achieving adequate margins is difficult.

evidence.snippet: The current standard of care involves upfront surgery for resectable tumors, with chemotherapy and radiation typically serving as adjuncts.

nodes.description: Leiomyosarcoma develops from smooth muscle cells or mesenchymal precursors committed to smooth-muscle differentiation. The disease most commonly arises in the retroperitoneum, uterus, and extremities.

evidence.snippet: Originating from either smooth muscle cells or their mesenchymal cell precursors, leiomyosarcoma primarily occurs in the retroperitoneum, uterus, and extremities, in descending order of frequency.

nodes.description: Leiomyosarcoma presents as an aggressive soft tissue tumor arising from smooth muscle-bearing or smooth-muscle-like anatomic sites, especially the pelvis, retroperitoneum, uterus, and extremities.

evidence.reference_title: Leiomyosarcoma: Current Clinical Management and Future Horizons.
evidence.snippet: Leiomyosarcomas are soft tissue tumors that are derived from smooth muscle mainly in the pelvis and retroperitoneum.

nodes.description: Complete surgical resection is the main curative-intent treatment for localized leiomyosarcoma and should be planned in experienced sarcoma centers.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis, prognosis, and management of leiomyosarcoma: recognition of anatomic variants.
evidence.snippet: Currently, the only curative option in LMS is surgery and despite progress in systemic therapy the outcome of patients with advanced/metastatic disease remains poor.

nodes.description: Leiomyosarcoma is a genetically complex sarcoma with recurrent loss of major tumor suppressor pathways rather than a single recurrent oncogenic fusion. Frequent alterations involve TP53, RB1, PTEN, and ATRX, with additional copy number gains such as MYOCD amplification in a subset of tumors.
nodes.id: Tumor Suppressor Loss and Genomic Complexity

evidence.reference_title: Targeted exome sequencing profiles genetic alterations in leiomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Losses of chromosomal regions involving key tumor suppressor genes PTEN (10q), RB1 (13q), CDH1 (16q), and TP53 (17p) were the most frequent genetic events.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted next-generation sequencing of cancer genes identified frequent TP53 and ATRX mutations in leiomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: In conclusion, we identified loss of function of the p53 and ATRX pathways being the main mechanisms for leiomyosarcomas.

nodes.description: Cell-cycle dysregulation drives persistent leiomyosarcoma growth. Recent data support an ESPL1-E2F1 proliferative axis that promotes tumor cell viability, genomic integrity under stress, and progression through G2/M.

evidence.reference_title: E2F1-mediated ESPL1 transcriptional activation predicts poor prognosis and promotes the proliferation of leiomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Functional studies in the LMS cell line SK-LMS-1 demonstrated that ESPL1 knockdown slowed cell proliferation and increased G2/M cell cycle arrest, suggesting its crucial role in maintaining LMS cell viability and genomic integrity.
